transcript: I'm gonna rank the stage performances of Jim Parsons, or at least the six of them that I've seen. I didn't see him in The Normal Heart or Harvey. And in sixth place, I do have his current performance in Titanique, which I just found pretty unfunny all around. On the complete opposite end of the spectrum, we have a man of no importance. Up until Titanique, Jim Parsons had kind of been doing the Daniel Radcliffe thing of, like, really trying to stretch himself in his stage roles. And this was maybe the most he stretched himself yet. A very valiant effort, but it didn't really work for me. Aside from the just-okay vocals and struggling with the dialect, he also played the role in a very brooding, understated way, which didn't really work. It ended up coming across more bland and charmless. In fourth place, his performance as the stage manager in our town, which I feel pretty neutral on honestly, for me, he was kind of just there. In third place, I have the boys in the band. A very respectable performance, though he was maybe a little miscast. I'm not sure if he quite captured the world weary cynicism of this character, but he still pretty much pulled off this tricky and meaty role. In second place, I have an act of god. Now, the show itself was, like, kinda okay. There were some groaner jokes, some funny jokes, but this was like Jim Parsons At his comedic peak, And I feel like it was well tailored to what he had to offer comedically. But easily in first place, I have his performance in Mother play, which I think was the best intersection of, like, the Jim Parsons shtick with the more dramatic, serious, emotional core that I think he's been chasing with a lot of his stage career. Parts of it were very whimsical. He had a great rapport with Celia Keenan-Bolger He effectively played the character at multiple different ages. And when the more serious, emotional turns came, he handled it very organically.
classificationReason: Creator ranks 6 Jim Parsons stage performances across multiple productions (Titanique, A Man of No Importance, Our Town, The Boys in the Band, etc.). Three or more shows with no single focus = roundup.
